essence: Devotion stands rule-free and self-young: undawned by method, unaged by road-dust, at home in the Lord's city, thriving on every ground (vv1-6).
Its ground proved: all beings love the self, the self is consciousness — so love stands on its own nature; knowing this by drowning is conquest (v7).

Consequences drawn: the world turns ritual ground, joy/sorrow/bewilderment all become the road, special-state localization is the one cheat — closing with the pain-seed mind ripened to freedom's fruit (vv8-26).

sections.SUMMARY: It establishes devotion without preparatory rule as valid, then proves it: since all beings desire the self and the self alone is consciousness, love directed at it stands on its own nature and needs no external ground. Knowing this by immersion is itself the conquest. The remaining verses draw the consequences — the world becomes ritual ground, every road works, localization of the goal in special states is the one deceit — and close by transfiguring the opening image: the dust-greyed mind, watered by devotion, fruits liberation.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of establishment (pratiṣṭhā); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at devotion without preparatory rule. The rasa is the tranquility of methodless devotion — not a means among means but the thing itself. Abhinava's rasa theory frames this as bhakti-rasa: the relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute as the sole beloved. Kṣemarāja's commentary: devotion without preparatory rule is valid because all beings desire the self and the self alone is consciousness.
